summary: A 1930 BC Forest Service report, as quoted by Canada Lookouts, records a temporary lookout developed on Hellroar Peak. Nothing later found.

events.note: Temporary lookout developed, with $173.00 spent on improvements, per the 1930 BC Forest Service annual report as quoted by Canada Lookouts. Not recorded as built because the source says developed; the annual report itself was not read.

notes_for_editor: One dated fact, secondhand: the 1930 line on the Canada Lookouts page, which cites the BC Forest Service annual report for 1930. I did not find or read the report itself. The source says 'developed', not built, so the event is recorded as other with a note; a human may want to check the report. The record's coordinates (52.2182, -119.1813) do not appear as text on the page; they come from the map embed in the page HTML. The federal gazetteer's Hellroar Mountain point (52.2188889, -119.1555555) is about 1.8 km east of the record point. Flag only, not a correction. A Facebook group post listed in search results, titled 'Hellroar Ridge fire lookout tower construction and relocation story' (dated 27 Aug 2023 in the snippet), could not be read, so nothing from it is used; it may bear on the site's history, the Peak/Ridge naming and any relocation. Access, status and staffing are unknown. Searches: two web searches. Fact-check 2026-10-20: the story now says the lookout was developed, not established, to match the source.
